title: Best Sum of Distinct Survivors
statement:
You get an integer array nums. You may delete any elements you like, as long as at least one element stays. The elements that survive must all be different values.

Return the largest possible sum of the surviving elements.

examples.why: Keep one 3 and the 5. The −1 only lowers the sum, and the second 3 is not allowed.
Every value is negative, but you cannot delete everything. Keep the single largest value.
Nothing is positive, so keep a single 0. The two zeros are equal values, so only one of them may stay.

hints: Deleting elements means you are choosing a subset, not a contiguous piece. What does a negative value ever do for the sum?
Keep each positive value once and drop everything else. Duplicates of a positive value cannot both stay, and one copy is all you need.
One case breaks that rule: if nothing is positive, the empty set is not allowed. Then keep the single largest element.

explain.intuition:
Since you can delete anything, you are just choosing a set of distinct values. Each positive value raises the sum, so take every positive value exactly once. Negative values only lower it, and zero changes nothing.

The one trap is the rule that something must survive. If the array has no positive value, the greedy choice would be "keep nothing". Then the best you can do is keep the single largest element, which is the least negative one, or 0 if there is a 0.
steps: Otherwise put every positive value into a set, so each counts once.
Return the sum of the set.
pitfalls: Returning 0 for an all-negative array. The empty selection is not allowed.
Adding every positive element, including duplicates: [2, 2, 2, 2] must give 2, not 8.
Reading the task as a contiguous subarray problem and reaching for a sliding window. Deletions can remove elements from the middle.

solutions.title: Try every set of distinct values
solutions.idea: Collect the distinct values and try every non-empty subset of them. Only usable when there are few distinct values.
solutions.time: O(2^d · d) for d distinct values

solutions.title: Greedy: every positive value once
solutions.idea: If anything is positive, the answer is the sum of the distinct positive values. Otherwise it is the maximum element.

followups: The survivors must now form a contiguous subarray with distinct values. Which technique do you need?
Values are between −100 and 100. How could a fixed-size boolean array replace the set?
